title: As...As
description: Describe equal and unequal qualities in two options.
objectives: Describe equal and unequal qualities in two options.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to describe equal and unequal qualities in two options. The central language is as adjective as and not as adjective as. It belongs to the practical context of comparing & choosing. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: as adjective as and not as adjective as

blocks.english: The small model is as fast as the large one.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the as...as exchange.

blocks.english: The bus isn't as convenient as the train.
blocks.explanation: This as...as model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the as...as exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “The small model is as fast as the large one.” and “The bus isn't as convenient as the train.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: as adjective as and not as adjective as.

Which option do you prefer? I prefer this one because it fits my needs.
The bus isn't as convenient as the train. Which option do you prefer?
